tasks.title: Negative indexes
tasks.statement: Python: l[-k]. Write from_end(v: &[i32], k: usize) -> Option<i32>: the k-th element from the end (k = 1 is the last). For k = 0 or k > len, return None.

tasks.title: Cyclic shift
tasks.statement: Python: l[k:] + l[:k]. Write rotate_left(v: &[i32], k: usize) -> Vec<i32>: shift left by k (k may be larger than the length).
tasks.hint: First k %= len, then concatenate the two slices.

tasks.title: Slice with a step
tasks.statement: Python: l[::2]. Write every_other(v: &[i32]) -> Vec<i32>: the elements at even indexes 0, 2, 4, …

tasks.title: list.remove(x)
tasks.statement: Python: l.remove(x) deletes the first occurrence and raises ValueError if there is none. Write remove_first(v: &mut Vec<i32>, x: i32) -> bool: true if something was removed.
tasks.hint: position gives the index of the first one, remove(i) deletes it.

tasks.title: Remove all
tasks.statement: Python: [x for x in l if x != v]. Write remove_all(v: &mut Vec<i32>, x: i32) — remove all occurrences in a single pass, using retain.

tasks.title: Unique, keeping order
tasks.statement: Python: list(dict.fromkeys(l)). Write unique(v: &[i32]) -> Vec<i32>: remove duplicates, keeping the order of first occurrences. No HashSet (only a vector and contains).

tasks.title: Batches
tasks.statement: Write batches(v: &[i32], n: usize) -> Vec<Vec<i32>>: split into batches of n elements (the last may be shorter), n > 0. Use chunks.

tasks.title: Sliding window
tasks.statement: Write moving_sums(v: &[i32], k: usize) -> Vec<i32>: the sums of all windows of k consecutive elements (k > 0). Use windows.
tasks.hint: windows(k) yields slices of length k.

tasks.title: Is it sorted
tasks.statement: Write is_sorted(v: &[i32]) -> bool: the elements are non-decreasing. Use windows(2).
tasks.hint: all on an empty sequence is true.

tasks.title: sorted(reverse=True)
tasks.statement: Python: sorted(l, reverse=True). Write sorted_desc(v: &[i32]) -> Vec<i32> — a sorted copy in descending order; the original slice is not changed.

tasks.title: key=len
tasks.statement: Python: sorted(words, key=len). Write by_len(words: &[&str]) -> Vec<String>: the words in increasing length in characters; for equal lengths, in the original order.

tasks.title: Top-k
tasks.statement: Python: sorted(l, reverse=True)[:k]. Write top_k(v: &[i32], k: usize) -> Vec<i32>: the k largest in descending order (if there are fewer elements, all of them).

tasks.title: bisect
tasks.statement: Python: bisect.bisect_left(l, x). Write insert_pos(v: &[i32], x: i32) -> usize: the position where to insert x to keep the order (to the left of equal ones). The slice is sorted. Use partition_point.

tasks.title: zip
tasks.statement: Python: list(zip(a, b)). Write pairs(a: &[i32], b: &[&str]) -> Vec<(i32, String)>: pairs up to the length of the shorter of the two slices.

tasks.title: Indexes from the end
tasks.statement: Write last_index_of(v: &[i32], x: i32) -> Option<usize>: the index of the last occurrence of x, or None. Use iter().rposition.

tasks.title: Flatten lists
tasks.statement: Python: [x for row in rows for x in row]. Write flatten(rows: &[Vec<i32>]) -> Vec<i32>.

tasks.title: Transpose
tasks.statement: Python: list(zip(*m)). Write transpose(m: &[Vec<i32>]) -> Vec<Vec<i32>> for a rectangular matrix (all rows have the same length; an empty matrix gives an empty result).

tasks.title: The [[0]*n]*m trap
tasks.statement: Write make_grid(rows: usize, cols: usize) -> Vec<Vec<i32>> filled with zeros; the rows are independent. After the call the driver changes one cell, and only one row changes.

tasks.title: Flat matrix
tasks.statement: A matrix is stored in one vector row by row, with width w. Write get(m: &[i32], w: usize, row: usize, col: usize) -> Option<i32>: the element, or None if out of bounds (col ≥ w or the index is past the end).
tasks.hint: The index is row * w + col; check col < w separately.

tasks.title: Bracket stack
tasks.statement: Write balanced(s: &str) -> bool: whether the brackets ()[]{} are placed correctly (use a Vec as a stack).
tasks.hint: push the opening ones, pop and compare for the closing ones.

tasks.title: Queue on VecDeque
tasks.statement: Write josephus(n: usize, k: usize) -> usize: the Josephus problem — n people in a circle, every k-th one is eliminated; return the number (from 1) of the last one left. Use VecDeque.
tasks.hint: Move k - 1 times from the front to the back, then remove.

tasks.title: Shortest path on a grid
tasks.statement: Write shortest(grid: &[&str]) -> Option<usize>: the length of the shortest path from 'S' to 'E' over the '.' cells (up, down, left, right), where '#' is a wall. None if there is no path. Breadth-first search on a VecDeque.
tasks.hint: dist stores the distances; the queue is a VecDeque of cells.

tasks.title: k-th largest
tasks.statement: Python: heapq.nlargest(k, l)[-1]. Write kth_largest(v: &[i32], k: usize) -> Option<i32>: the k-th largest (k = 1 is the largest) using BinaryHeap. None if k = 0 or k > len.
tasks.hint: BinaryHeap is a max-heap; pop gives the largest.

tasks.title: Vector capacity
tasks.statement: Write growth(n: usize) -> Vec<usize>: create an empty Vec<u8>, add n elements, and record capacity() in the result every time it changes (no consecutive repeats). For the first n = 20 the result will be strictly increasing.
tasks.hint: Remember the capacity after each push and compare it with the last one.

tasks.title: Split in half
tasks.statement: Write halves(v: &[i32]) -> (Vec<i32>, Vec<i32>): the left half (length len / 2) and the right (the rest). Use split_at.

tasks.title: Pull out a range
tasks.statement: Write cut(v: &mut Vec<i32>, a: usize, b: usize) -> Vec<i32>: remove the elements a..b from v and return them (drain).

tasks.title: Index of the maximum
tasks.statement: Python: l.index(max(l)). Write argmax(v: &[i32]) -> Option<usize>: the index of the first largest element, or None for an empty slice.
tasks.hint: A strict comparison keeps the index of the first one.

tasks.title: Prefix sums
tasks.statement: Python: list(itertools.accumulate(l)). Write prefix_sums(v: &[i32]) -> Vec<i32>: partial sums (the i-th element is the sum of the first i + 1).
tasks.hint: A closure can change an outer variable s.

tasks.title: Two numbers with a given sum
tasks.statement: Write two_sum(v: &[i32], target: i32) -> Option<(usize, usize)>: indexes i < j with v[i] + v[j] = target (the first pair found when iterating i, then j).
tasks.hint: Two nested loops, j starts at i + 1.

tasks.title: Merge sorted
tasks.statement: Write merge(a: &[i32], b: &[i32]) -> Vec<i32>: merge two sorted slices into one sorted vector in linear time (with two indexes).
tasks.hint: After the loop, append the tails of both slices.
